'''''Bidens pilosa''''' is an annual species of [[herbaceous]] flowering plant in the daisy family [[Asteraceae]]. Its many common names include '''hitch hikers''', '''black-jack''', '''beggarticks''', '''farmer's friends''' and '''Spanish needle''', but most commonly referred to as '''cobblers pegs'''. It is native to the [[Americas]] but is widely distributed as an [[introduced species]] in other regions including [[Eurasia]], [[Africa]], [[Australia]], [[South America]] and the [[Pacific Islands]],<ref name="pier">[http://www.hear.org/pier/species/bidens_pilosa.htm ''Bidens pilosa''.] Pacific Island Ecosystems at Risk (PIER). USFS.</ref> and is classified as an [[invasive species]] in some regions of the world.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Stohlgren |first1=Thomas J. |last2=Pyšek |first2=Petr |last3=Kartesz |first3=John |last4=Nishino |first4=Misako |last5=Pauchard |first5=Aníbal |last6=Winter |first6=Marten |last7=Pino |first7=Joan |last8=Richardson |first8=David M. |last9=Wilson |first9=John |last10=Murray |first10=Brad R. |last11=Phillips |first11=Megan L. |last12=Celesti-Grapow |first12=Laura |last13=Graham |first13=Jim |title=Encyclopedia of Biodiversity |chapter=Globalization Effects on Common Plant Species |date=2013 |pages=700–706 |doi=10.1016/B978-0-12-384719-5.00239-2 |isbn=978-0-12-384720-1 }}</ref><ref name="WeedId">{{Cite web |title=Cobbler's pegs |url=https://weeds.brisbane.qld.gov.au/weeds/cobblers-pegs |access-date=2024-03-16 |website=Weed Identification – Brisbane City Council |language=en}}</ref>

==Description==
''Bidens pilosa'' is a branched annual [[forb]] of [[Gracility|gracile]] [[Habit (biology)|habit]], growing up to {{Convert|1.8|m|sp=us}} tall. It grows aggressively on [[Disturbance (ecology)|disturbed]] land and often becomes weedy. The leaves are all [[Leaf|oppositely arranged]] and range from simple to [[pinnate]] in form, the upper leaves with three to five [[Leaf|dentate]], [[Leaf shape|ovate]]-to-[[Leaf shape|lanceolate]] leaflets. The [[Petiole (botany)|petiole]]s are slightly winged.<ref name=r>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=200023537 Flora of North America, ''Bidens pilosa'' Linnaeus, Sp. Pl. 2: 832. 1753. ]</ref>

The plant may flower at any time of the year, but mainly in summer and autumn in temperate regions. The flowers are small [[pseudanthium|heads]] borne on relatively long [[Peduncle (botany)|peduncles]]. The heads consist of about four or five broad white [[ray florets]] (ligules),  surrounding many tubular yellow [[disc floret]]s without ligules that develop into barbed fruits.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Spanish needles: definition of Spanish needles in Oxford dictionary (American English) (US)|url = http://www.oxforddictionaries.com/us/definition/american_english/spanish-needles?q=spanish+needles|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20151208232003/http://www.oxforddictionaries.com/us/definition/american_english/spanish-needles?q=spanish+needles|url-status = dead|archive-date = December 8, 2015|website = www.oxforddictionaries.com|access-date = 2016-02-11}}</ref>

The fruits are slightly curved, stiff, rough black rods, tetragonal in cross section, about 1 cm long, typically with two to three stiff, heavily barbed [[Awn (botany)|awns]] at their [[Anatomical terms of location|distal]] ends.

The [[infructescence]]s form [[wikt:stellate|stellate]] spherical [[bur]]rs about one to two centimeters in diameter. The barbed spines of the achenes get stuck in the feathers, fur, fleeces, clothing, or any other parts of people or animals that brush against the plant.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Plant Discoveries Sherwin Carlquist Island Biology LOSS of DISPERSIBILITY on ISLANDS|url = http://www.sherwincarlquist.com/loss-of-dispersibility-on-islands.html|website = www.sherwincarlquist.com|access-date = 2016-02-11|archive-date = 2016-03-04|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160304140447/http://www.sherwincarlquist.com/loss-of-dispersibility-on-islands.html|url-status = dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title = beggarticks: definition of beggarticks in Oxford dictionary (American English) (US)|url = http://www.oxforddictionaries.com/us/definition/american_english/beggarticks?q=beggars+ticks|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20151209000759/http://www.oxforddictionaries.com/us/definition/american_english/beggarticks?q=beggars+ticks|url-status = dead|archive-date = December 9, 2015|website = www.oxforddictionaries.com|access-date = 2016-02-11}}</ref> 
It is an effective means of [[seed dispersal]] by [[zoochory]], as the fruits are transported by animals. 

This mechanism has helped the plant become a [[noxious weed]] in temperate and tropical regions.<ref name="WeedId" /><ref name="r" /><ref>{{Cite web|title = *Bidens pilosa — Noosa's Native Plants|url = http://noosanativeplants.com.au/plants/942/*bidens-pilosa|website = noosanativeplants.com.au|access-date = 2016-02-11|first = Acura|last = Multimedia|archive-date = 2016-02-28|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160228010632/http://noosanativeplants.com.au/plants/942/*bidens-pilosa|url-status = dead}}</ref> It is susceptible to hand weeding if small enough. Even then it must be bagged, and thick mulches may prevent it from growing.<ref name="grubben">{{cite book |editor1-last=Grubben |editor1-first=G. J. H. |editor2-last=Denton |editor2-first=O. A. |title=Vegetables |date=2004 |publisher=PROTA |isbn=978-90-5782-147-9 |page=115 |oclc=57724930 |url=https://edepot.wur.nl/417517 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Sustainable Horse Keeping |url=http://goldcoasthorse.com.au/Gold_Coast_Horse/Sustainable_Horse_Keeping.html |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20151208231046/http://goldcoasthorse.com.au/Gold_Coast_Horse/Sustainable_Horse_Keeping.html |archivedate=2015-12-08 |access-date=2016-02-11 |website=goldcoasthorse.com.au}}</ref>

==Distribution==
The species is native to tropical America, widely naturalized throughout the warm temperate and tropical regions of the world.<ref name=bionet>{{cite web|title=Bidens pilosa (Blackjack)|work=BioNET EAFRINET Keys and Factsheets| url=https://keys.lucidcentral.org/keys/v3/eafrinet/weeds/key/weeds/Media/Html/Bidens_pilosa_(Blackjack).htm |access-date=2020-03-25}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Factsheet - Bidens pilosa |url=http://keyserver.lucidcentral.org/weeds/data/080c0106-040c-4508-8300-0b0a06060e01/media/Html/Bidens_pilosa.htm |website=keyserver.lucidcentral.org |access-date=2016-02-11 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305103457/http://keyserver.lucidcentral.org/weeds/data/080c0106-040c-4508-8300-0b0a06060e01/media/Html/Bidens_pilosa.htm |archivedate=2016-03-05}}</ref> A weed of gardens, woodlands and waste areas.<ref name="survival.org.au">{{Cite web|title = Bidens pilosa - Cobbler's Pegs - Edible Weeds and Bush Tucker Plant Foods|url = http://www.survival.org.au/bf_bidens_pilosa.php|website = www.survival.org.au|access-date = 2016-02-11}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title = Dangars Falls and Salisbury Waters|url = http://www.donsmaps.com/salisbury.html|website = www.donsmaps.com|access-date = 2016-02-11}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title = Elizabeth and Rob|url = http://elizabeth-nowell.blogspot.com.es/|website = elizabeth-nowell.blogspot.com.es|access-date = 2016-02-11}}</ref>

==Common names==
Its many English common names include black-jack,<ref name=Stace>{{cite book|last=Stace|first=C. A.|authorlink = Stace, C. A.|year=2019|title=New Flora of the British Isles|edition=Fourth|publisher=C & M Floristics|location = Middlewood Green, Suffolk, U.K.| isbn=978-1-5272-2630-2}}</ref>{{rp|819}} beggarticks, hairy beggarticks, cobbler's pegs, devil's needles, hairy bidens, Spanish needle, farmers friend, devil's pitchfork, hitch hikers and sticky beaks.<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007|accessdate=2014-10-17}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.survival.org.au/bf_bidens_pilosa.php | title=Wilderness Survival, Tracking, and Awareness}}</ref><ref>[http://bie.ala.org.au/species/urn:lsid:biodiversity.org.au:apni.taxon:565633# Atlas of Living Australia,  Bidens pilosa L., Cobbler's Peg]</ref>

==Uses==
Although ''Bidens pilosa'' is primarily considered a [[weed]], in many parts of the world it is also a source of [[food]] and [[alternative medicine]].<ref name="prota">Grubben, G. J. H. & O. A. Denton. (2004) Plant Resources of Tropical Africa 2. Vegetables. PROTA Foundation, Wageningen; Backhuys, Leiden; CTA, Wageningen.</ref> The leaves have a resinous flavor and are eaten raw or in stews or dried for storage. In eastern Africa it is used for medicinal purposes to treat wounds.<ref>{{cite book |editor1-last= Prance |editor1-first=Ghillean |editor2-last=Nesbitt |editor2-first=Mark |last1=Pieroni |first1=Andrea |date=2005 |chapter=Gathering food from the wild |title=The Cultural History of Plants |publisher=Routledge |page=31 |isbn=0415927463}}</ref> Extracts from ''Bidens pilosa'' are used in southern Africa for malaria.<ref name="grubben" />

During the Vietnam War, soldiers{{which|date=December 2021}} adopted the herb as a vegetable, which led to it being known as the "soldier vegetable".<ref>{{ cite book | first1=Yoshitaka | last1=Tanaka | first2=Nguyen | last2=Van Ke | date=2007 | title=Edible Wild Plants of Vietnam: The Bountiful Garden | publisher=Orchid Press | location=Thailand | isbn=978-9745240896 | page=38}}</ref>

==Chemistry==
Almost 200 compounds have been isolated from ''B. pilosa'', especially [[Polyyne|polyacetylene]]s and [[flavonoid]]s.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lima Silva |first1=Fabiana |last2=Fischer |first2=Dominique Corinne Hermine |last3=Fechine Tavares |first3=Josean |last4=Sobral Silva |first4=Marcelo |last5=Filgueiras de Athayde-Filho |first5=Petronio |last6=Barbosa-Filho |first6=Jose Maria |title=Compilation of Secondary Metabolites from Bidens pilosa L. |journal=Molecules |date=26 January 2011 |volume=16 |issue=2 |pages=1070–1102 |doi=10.3390/molecules16021070 |pmid=21270729 |pmc=6259624 |doi-access=free }}</ref> The plant contains [[ethyl caffeate]], a [[hydroxycinnamic acid]].<ref name=Chiang>{{cite journal |last1=Chiang |first1=Yi-Ming |last2=Lo |first2=Chiu-Ping |last3=Chen |first3=Yi-Ping |last4=Wang |first4=Sheng-Yang |last5=Yang |first5=Ning-Sun |last6=Kuo |first6=Yueh-Hsiung |last7=Shyur |first7=Lie-Fen |title=Ethyl caffeate suppresses NF- κ B activation and its downstream inflammatory mediators, iNOS, COX-2, and PGE 2 in vitro or in mouse skin |journal=British Journal of Pharmacology |date=October 2005 |volume=146 |issue=3 |pages=352–363 |doi=10.1038/sj.bjp.0706343 |pmid=16041399 |pmc=1576288 }}</ref>
